meta.tagline: 2,500-year-old walls, Adriatic coves and a coastline that never sleeps

pills: One of the Adriatic's oldest towns
History by day, party by night

overview.title: Welcome to Budva
overview.intro: Budva is a two-faced coastal beauty: inside the stone walls, 2,500 years of Mediterranean memory; outside them, the liveliest riviera on the Adriatic. Washing lines and church bells in the narrow lanes in the morning, emerald coves at noon, endless music along the shore at night. Few cities change character so many times over such short distances — so change with it: be a historian in the morning, a swimmer at noon, a dinner guest in the evening.

local_word.definition: 'Slowly, no hurry': the one-word summary of the Montenegrin philosophy of life. Waiter running late, ferry delayed? The answer is always the same: polako. Accept it and it's a holiday; resist it and it's stress.

rules.title: Live the Old Town at morning and dusk
rules.description: Stari Grad surrenders to tour groups at midday; the stone lanes show their real face at 8 am and after sunset. Lose yourself inside the walls at those hours, and throw yourself into the sea at noon.

rules.title: Beach does not mean sunbed
rules.description: In summer the front-row sunbed sets ask serious money; yet every beach has a free towel zone and the sea is the same for everyone. Don't sit without asking, don't lie down without reading the price.

rules.title: Sveti Stefan is for looking, not entering
rules.description: The postcard island is a private hotel; entry is reserved for staying guests and at times it is closed entirely. Spare yourself the disappointment: the real magic is the silhouette seen from the opposite slope anyway.

quick_facts.label: Money
quick_facts.sub: Uses the euro without being in the EU

tip.label: The Budva philosophy
tip.text: Think of Budva not as one town but as a riviera: a cove in the morning, another village at noon, the Old Town at night. The best moments are caught between two stops, on the coastal path.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: The centre is entirely walkable; for the riviera's coves and villages there are minibuses, boats and short taxi hops.

items.title: Airport to the centre
items.description: Tivat airport is 20 minutes away: fix the taxi price before getting in, or use a ride app. Coming from Podgorica, the mountain road is a small scenic tour of its own — about an hour.

items.title: The riviera buses
items.description: Minibuses shuttle all day along the Budva–Bečići–Rafailovići–Sveti Stefan line: cheap, frequent and used to beach bags. Intercity buses to Petrovac and Kotor leave from the main terminal.

items.title: The seafront promenade on foot
items.description: The coastal walk from the Old Town to Bečići takes 40 minutes through tunnels and paths: sea on one side, pine scent on the other. The rocky path to Mogren beach is the town's most beautiful 15 minutes.

items.title: Boat taxis and tours
items.description: Boats from the harbour reach Sveti Nikola island ('Hawaii') in ten minutes; day tours stretch to the Bay of Kotor and the blue cave. The price list is posted on the boat — read it before boarding.

items.title: A rental car — for cove hunting
items.description: The riviera's hidden coves (Kraljičina, Drobni Pijesak) open up by car; but in summer parking is worth gold and the single-lane coast road drowns in traffic. Leave early, don't return at noon.

callout.label: Minibus tip
callout.text: For the Sveti Stefan view, get off not at the village entrance but at the hairpin stop on the main road above: the postcard angle is there — photo first, then walk down.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Budva the question is: do you want to be close to the stone of the walls, the sand of the beach, or the riviera's quiet villages?

local_word.definition: A traditional family tavern of stone walls and wooden tables: fish on the grill, wine in the jug, and a bill that feels like it came from a friend. In Montenegro, the safest answer to 'where shall we eat' is always a konoba.

items.name: Stari Grad (the Old Town)
items.description: Waking up in stone houses inside the walls: church bells, narrow lanes, Mogren beach two steps away. In summer the night music drifts over the walls — a little noise is the price of the romance.

items.name: The Slovenska Plaža strip
items.description: The belt of hotels and apartments behind the long town beach: right on the sea, plenty of restaurants, a wide price range. In July and August it has the rhythm of a lively resort town — light sleepers should pick upper floors.

items.name: Bečići
items.description: The riviera's award-winning sand: a broad beach, big resorts and an easy setup for families. A 10-minute walk to Budva through the tunnel — sand by day, Old Town by night is an easy combination.

items.name: Rafailovići
items.description: A small cove that keeps its old fishing-village fabric: konobas on the shore, quiet evenings, fairly priced apartments. The base for those after a fish dinner + the sound of the sea.

items.name: Pržno and around Sveti Stefan
items.description: The slopes facing the postcard island: olive groves, small beaches, boutique stays. At a distance from Budva's noise, next door to the riviera's most photogenic sunset.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Budva's calendar is built around the sea: May-June and September are gold, July-August crowded but exuberant.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Pre-Season Paradise
items.subtitle: Spring · Empty beaches, the sea warming up
items.description: In May the sea is cool but swimmable, the beaches half empty, the prices friendly. June is the peak of balance: everything open, the crowds not yet arrived, evenings long on the terrace.

callout.label: June tip
callout.text: Mid-June is the riviera's best fortnight: the sea has warmed, the sunbeds are calm, and a konoba table needs no haggling. Set the year's booking here.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Riviera Peak
items.subtitle: Summer · Festival season, nightlife, full beaches
items.description: The region's two liveliest months: beaches full, the shore nights stretched by concerts and festivals, the Old Town's squares turned into theatre stages. Don't come without bookings, and don't survive without polako.

callout.label: August note
callout.text: In August the sunbeds run out by 9 am and the coast road locks up at noon. Go to the beach early, use the minibus-and-boat pair instead of a car, and reserve your dinner table.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Warm Sea, Calm Shore
items.subtitle: Autumn · September swimming, October walking
items.description: September belongs to those in the know: the sea still holds summer's warmth, the crowds are gone, the prices are down. In October swimming is for the determined, but the coastal paths and mountain villages open their golden hiking season.

callout.label: September tip
callout.text: In September go to Mogren in the morning and have the beach almost to yourself; in the afternoon hop on the Sveti Nikola boat — the boats that queued all summer are now a chat with the captain.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Curtain Down, Stone Open
items.subtitle: Winter · Silent walls, local life
items.description: The riviera goes into hibernation: some hotels close and the shore is left to the locals. The Old Town is photogenic even in the rain and prices hit the year's floor — but look for the beach-town spirit in summer.

callout.label: February note
callout.text: If you come in winter, give a sunny day to Kotor and the mountain village of Njeguši: while Budva's shore is silent, the bay and a pršut tasting know no season.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Montenegrin table is a marriage of two worlds: the Mediterranean's fish and olive oil on the coast, the mountain's meat, cheese and rakija two hours inland.

local_word.definition: Small fried dough puffs served hot: eaten with honey, cheese or jam. The guest offering of Montenegrin homes — if you see them on a konoba breakfast menu, order without hesitation.

items.name: Crni rižoto — black risotto
items.description: Jet-black risotto cooked in cuttlefish ink: the signature plate of the Adriatic coast. Your teeth go dark and nobody minds — squeeze the lemon, let white wine keep it company.
items.tag: At a seafront konoba · with lemon

items.name: Grilled fish, by the gram
items.description: In konobas the fish is chosen from the display and charged by weight: sea bass, bream or the day's catch. Blitva (chard and potatoes) is the classic side; ask the price before the scales.
items.tag: Choose from the display · ask the per-kilo price

items.name: Njeguški pršut and sir
items.description: The smoke-dried ham and cheese of the mountain village of Njeguši: the heart of the Montenegrin meze. With olives and a glass of Vranac, it is the opening of the table.

items.name: Riblja čorba — fish soup
items.description: A dark, saffron-and-tomato soup made from the day's fish: the first plate after a long beach day. Dunking your bread isn't bad manners, it's the method.
items.tag: Evening starter · with plenty of bread

items.name: Priganice + honey + cheese
items.description: Fried dough puffs, the star of the village breakfast: sweet with honey, savoury with melting cheese. Mixing both on one plate is allowed — no rules, only appetite.

items.name: The Vranac and rakija ritual
items.description: Montenegro's dark red Vranac goes well with meat, with fish, even with solitude; the pre-dinner rakija (grape or plum) is the national opening move. Don't drink without saying 'Živjeli!'

callout.label: The konoba rule
callout.text: The seafront restaurant with a photo menu in eight languages works for tourists; the konoba with a handwritten daily menu works for you. The way to guarantee the fish is fresh is simple: ask 'what did you catch today?'

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone knows the beach; these six are the riviera's backstage.

items.rarity: Only by sea or by steps
items.name: Mogren II
items.description: Everyone stops at Mogren I; pass through the short tunnel in the rocks and the second, prettier cove opens. Before 9 am it's nearly private — if there's a swell, accept getting splashed in the tunnel.

items.name: The Ballerina statue rock
items.description: The graceful gymnast statue on the rock facing the Old Town carries the legend of the girl who waited for her sailor. The photo is a classic, but the real prize is the angle from the rock back towards the walls.

items.name: Kraljičina Plaža
items.description: The 'Queen's Beach' hidden beyond the Miločer woods: a small crown reached by a pine-shaded path. Combine the walk with the park path and its Sveti Stefan views — the riviera's most elegant half day.

items.name: Sveti Nikola island
items.description: The island locals call 'Hawaii' is ten minutes from the harbour: pebble coves, clear water and the Budva silhouette across the strait. Bring your umbrella and water — the island's magic lies in how little service there is.

items.name: The Citadela and walls walk
items.description: The fortress at the Old Town's tip hangs over the sea with its library and terrace: as the waves beat the stones, the Adriatic opens to the horizon. Go near sunset — the stone turns to gold.

items.name: Petrovac and Lučice
items.description: The calm town 20 minutes down the riviera: a stone fort, a pine-scented promenade and the small cove of Lučice. Tailor-made for an afternoon's escape from Budva's crowds.

callout.label: Path tip
callout.text: The seaside path and tunnel walk from Bečići to Rafailovići is the riviera's most pleasant 20 minutes: between them lie mini beaches reached by steps — on crowded days these are the real swimming spots.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: In summer Budva prices itself for tourists; know these four and both your budget and your mood survive.

items.name: Lying down on a sunbed without asking
items.description: Front-row sunbed sets reach serious figures in August, and once you've sat down there's no bargaining.
items.instead: Read the price board, or ask; or settle in the towel zone. Arrive before 9 am and on most beaches you'll get the front row at the normal price.

items.name: The night taxi with a 'broken' meter
items.description: Outside the clubs at night the meter is 'broken' and a short hop is quoted at an outrageous price.
items.instead: Fix the price before getting in, or use a ride app; if it's short, the promenade was built for walking anyway.

items.name: The beach club's 'free' sunbed
items.description: The beach club that says 'sunbeds free' explains the minimum spend after you've sat down; with two cocktails the bill reaches the price of a whole beach day.
items.instead: Ask the minimum spend before sitting. If you want music and a scene, choose it knowingly; if you just want the sea, the public beach two steps away offers the same water.

items.name: Dreaming of entering Sveti Stefan
items.description: Those who go expecting to tour the island are turned back at the gate: entry is for hotel guests only, and in closed periods not even for them.
items.instead: Watch the island from the hairpin viewpoint and the Miločer park path; if you have time, swim off the opposite beach and catch the finest angle from the sea.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: In Budva every summer price is born negotiable: sunbed, boat, taxi, sometimes even the room. A smiling 'what's the final price?' is the official language of this coast.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: From the walls to the cove, from the cove to the sunset

steps.title: Stari Grad, empty
steps.description: Stone lanes, the Citadela and the walls walk in the morning cool: before the tour groups arrive, the Old Town is yours. Start with a coffee on the square.

steps.title: The Mogren path and a swim
steps.description: Stop at the Ballerina statue, take the rocky path down to Mogren; pass through the tunnel to the second cove and take the day's first swim.

steps.title: Lunch at a konoba
steps.description: Back to the harbour: riblja čorba + grilled fish, or crni rižoto. Cold white wine alongside, boats for a view.

steps.title: The Sveti Nikola boat
steps.description: Ten minutes from the harbour to 'Hawaii': swim off the pebble cove and watch Budva's silhouette from across the water. Ice cream on the promenade on the way back.

steps.title: The Sveti Stefan view
steps.description: Minibus to the hairpin stop: the postcard island turns to gold in the sunset light. Walk down to Pržno for a glass by the water — the riviera's most elegant hour.

steps.title: An Old Town evening
steps.description: Dinner inside the walls, then square concerts or the bars under the ramparts: the night doesn't end early in Budva — you decide.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Collect the riviera cove by cove

steps.title: Classic Budva
steps.description: The one-day flow above: Old Town, Mogren, the island, the Sveti Stefan view.

steps.title: A Bay of Kotor escape
steps.description: Morning bus or tour to Kotor: climb the walls, boat to Perast and Our Lady of the Rocks; back to Budva for a fish dinner in Rafailovići.

steps.title: Coves and farewell
steps.description: Morning on the Miločer path to Kraljičina beach; lunch at a konoba in Petrovac + the Lučice cove; a farewell dinner in the Old Town and one last night walk under the walls.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Montenegrin's door opens with five words; the pronunciation is friendly and a smile is the shared language.

items.meaning: Good day — said entering a shop, a konoba, a bus
Thank you — 'hvala puno' means thanks a lot
Please / you're welcome / here you go — one word, three jobs
Cheers! — eye contact as the rakija rises is mandatory
Slowly, easy — Montenegro's philosophy of life; when you hear it, smile and adopt it

checklist.title: Budva Checklist
checklist.completion_message: Živjeli! You've done the riviera properly!

items.label: Walk Stari Grad empty in the morning
items.sub: Stone lanes and church bells, all yours

items.label: Look over the Adriatic from the Citadela
Pass the tunnel to Mogren II
items.sub: The second cove is always prettier

items.label: Take the boat to Sveti Nikola
Photograph Sveti Stefan from the hairpin

items.sub: Black teeth are part of the deal

items.label: Choose the day's fish at a konoba
items.sub: Don't forget to ask the per-kilo price

items.sub: 20 minutes of tunnels and mini coves
